Level 1: Grep assertion — for every tool name in build_tools(), `grep -F <tool_name> submodules/cua/libs/cua-bench/cua_bench/agents/openclaw/AGENTS.md` must return 0 matches. Any match is a regression.

Level 1: Grep assertion — every tool-specific operational string in prompt.py (tool names, target= values, flag names) must appear inside a function whose name matches `_build_*` and whose early-return condition references the same tool name. Flag any literal that appears outside a gated builder.

Level 1: Gating-correctness check — for each `_build_<tool>()` method, the tool names referenced in its output must be a subset of the tool names checked in its gating condition (prevents the `_build_memory_write`-style drift where prose mentions a tool the gate doesn't require).

Level 1: Unit tests pass — test_prompt.py must include a present/absent branch test for every `_build_<tool>()` method: assert `[] when gating tools absent`, assert expected header + key phrases present when gating tools registered.

Level 2: run_magic_tower.sh 50 — dump the rendered system prompt on turn 1 (prompt.py PromptBuilder.build() output) and assert: (a) every registered tool appears in the Tools list, (b) no prose mentions a tool that isn't in tool_summaries, (c) AGENTS.md content appears verbatim in Project Context with no tool-specific additions injected at render time.

Level 2: For each tool in the US-OC-031 backlog that OpenClaw has Layer 2 prose for but we do not (exec, update_plan, apply_patch, process per the tool-migration audit), file or update a follow-up ticket in prd.json capturing the missing `_build_<tool>()` method. Attach a code pointer to the OpenClaw prose.
Level 3 (optional): wire the grep and gating-correctness checks into CI as a lightweight pre-commit or PR check so the audit is self-enforcing between manual runs.
userStories.notes: Recurring hygiene story — re-run once after each new tool lands from the US-OC-031 backlog. Output is an audit doc + any filed follow-up tickets; no production code changes unless a drift is found. Four principles to enforce: (1) single source for tool prose — each tool's operational rules live in exactly one gated `_build_<tool>()`, never duplicated into AGENTS.md; (2) absence-is-the-signal — prose is gated on `"<tool>" in tool_summaries`, disabled tools produce silence, not a 'disabled' disclaimer; (3) AGENTS.md stays conceptual — workspace semantics, behavior, task-completion contract only, zero tool names or argument values; (4) BaseTool.description owns Layer 1 (one-line what-it-does), `_build_<tool>()` owns Layer 2 (non-obvious operational rules — polling, concurrency caps, format rules, target= argument semantics). The regression this guards against is real: prior to today, AGENTS.md had memory_write target='session'/'task_memory' prose that was moved into _build_memory() — a grep-based CI check would have prevented that from shipping.
